transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've failed. I feel like I failed as a father, and really just as a useful person in general. It just keeps looping in my head, over and over. It gets to the point where I honestly feel like I don't deserve much of a future.
Have you ever felt this way for a period of two weeks or more at any point in your life before this current stretch of time?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, like anyone else, but... never anything like this. I've never felt this low for weeks at a time before this current stretch. It's really the first time it's been this heavy.
How has this feeling affected your ability to carry out your daily activities, such as working or taking care of your basic responsibilities?

Well, it's pretty much brought everything to a halt. My bills and house projects are just piling up because I... I just can't make myself follow through on any of it. I've also stopped seeing the few people I used to count on, like at my book club or out on rides. I just don't go anymore. 

Honestly, I don't feel safe just brushing this off anymore. Especially recently... I started organizing my finances, putting all the paperwork in order like someone else might need to take them over soon. That's when I realized I really needed to come in.
Are you currently experiencing any physical symptoms, such as a complete loss of appetite, significant weight loss, or an inability to sleep or wake up at your usual times?

Well, my appetite is pretty much gone. Most days I don't even bother making a real meal anymore. I just... I forget to eat until it's late in the day, and even then, I can only really manage some toast or a bowl of cereal. Because of that, yeah, I have lost some weight. I've actually had to tighten my belt recently just to keep my pants up.
Have you noticed if you are moving or speaking much more slowly than usual, or conversely, feeling so restless that you cannot sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel like I'm moving or talking any slower than normal. And I'm definitely not feeling restless or like I can't sit still. I just... I feel heavy, but my movements and speech seem pretty much the same as they always have been.
